subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Politically Exposed Persons
description: A quick win: understand Politically Exposed Persons.

hook.text: A foreign minister opens an account with $50 million. Where does a government official get that kind of money?

buildup.text: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) hold positions that make them vulnerable to corruption and bribery.

discovery.text: Banks must identify PEPs and apply enhanced monitoring to their accounts and family members.

twist.text: PEP screening is difficult. Databases are incomplete, names vary across languages, and roles change constantly.

climax.text: PEP controls exist because power and corruption go hand in hand. High office demands high scrutiny.

punchline.text: Power attracts corruption. PEP rules follow the money.

quiz.question: Why do banks apply extra scrutiny to PEPs?
options: Their positions make them vulnerable to corruption
They are exempt from normal banking rules
